findings.claim: A memorycard mem_search or mem_context with no `project` argument is denied for any session bound to a running workflow. This is the call memorycard makes by default, because it resolves the project from the working directory. It reuses the Engram rule (checkEngramProject) that a read naming no project is denied. Memorycard has a different default from Engram, so the common bare call is blocked, not only cross-project reads.
evidence: The diff registers memorycardProjectReadTool with check: checkEngramProject (gate.go lines 311-312 of the diff).
engramProjectGate returns Deny when read.Project == "" ('names no project (the project argument is missing, not a string, or empty)').
The user's global instructions state that memorycard resolves the project from the working directory when `project` is not passed. So the bare call is legitimate and is now denied.
The commit's tests only cover a call that passes `project`. The no-project denial for memorycard is not shown to be intended.
